task: R1 must reach 2001:db8:20::/64 through adjacent router fe80::2 on GigabitEthernet0/0. Add the IPv6 route with the necessary local-link scope.

teaching.hint: A link-local next hop cannot identify its link from the address alone.
teaching.takeaway: The exit interface scopes fe80::2 to the intended neighbor. Correct syntax can still fail if that address belongs to the peer on a different link.

task: Global next hop 2001:db8:12::2 is reachable through R1's connected transit prefix. Add a next-hop-only route to 2001:db8:20::/64 through it.

teaching.hint: A global next hop can be resolved through another installed route.
teaching.takeaway: Unlike a link-local next hop, this address can be resolved without an explicit interface in the static command. Verify that its resolving route remains usable; configuration alone is insufficient.

task: For IPv6 destinations with no more-specific match, use neighbor fe80::2 on R1 GigabitEthernet0/0. Add that default route.

teaching.hint: Use the IPv6 zero-length prefix and retain the link-local interface scope.
teaching.takeaway: ::/0 is the IPv6 default. More-specific installed routes still win, and the default cannot provide a missing downstream or return path.

task: Only host 2001:db8:20::12 must use fe80::3 on R1 GigabitEthernet0/1. Add an IPv6 host route while preserving the wider LAN route.

teaching.hint: The destination length must identify exactly one 128-bit address.
teaching.takeaway: A /128 affects one host and wins over a matching /64 when installed. The interface scopes the link-local next hop; it does not change which destination the prefix matches.

task: The preferred route to 2001:db8:20::/64 has distance 1. Add a standby through fe80::3 on GigabitEthernet0/1 at distance 5.

teaching.hint: Preserve the same destination prefix and place the less-preferred distance last.
teaching.takeaway: A higher distance creates a standby only against a better candidate for the same prefix. The backup must also have a usable scoped neighbor and a working return path.

task: Primary and floating IPv6 static routes are configured. Display only the static routes currently installed on R1.

teaching.hint: Choose the IPv6 installed table, not the configuration file.
teaching.takeaway: An unselected floating route can remain configured without appearing here. Compare the selected distance and scoped next hop during the separate failure and recovery phases.

task: R1 has both a /64 LAN route and a /128 exception. Request the IPv6 route entry covering 2001:db8:20::12 to check which one handles that destination.

teaching.hint: Query the destination address; do not choose the mask in advance.
teaching.takeaway: The returned /128 is the more-specific match if installed, even when its distance is larger than the /64's. Next-hop resolution and a return route still determine whether the test succeeds.
